subject: maths
title: Mental Addition and Subtraction
seo_title: Year 3 Mental Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: Add and Subtract Ones, Tens and Hundreds
standard_text: Add and subtract numbers mentally, including: a three-digit number and ones; a three-digit number and tens; a three-digit number and hundreds.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on mental addition and subtraction: add and subtract ones, tens and hundreds to a three-digit number, cross a ten or a hundred, find missing numbers and solve word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Find the digit that changes: ones, tens or hundreds.
key_sub: 342 + 5 = 347, 342 + 50 = 392 and 342 + 500 = 842. If the digit goes past 9, cross to the next ten or hundred: 347 + 6 = 353.
body_html:
Which digit changes?

When you add or take away ones, the ones digit changes. With tens, the tens digit changes. With hundreds, the hundreds digit changes. The other digits stay the same.

CalculationAnswerWhat changes
342 + 5347the ones: 2 + 5 = 7
342 + 50392the tens: 4 + 5 = 9
342 + 500842the hundreds: 3 + 5 = 8
768 − 300468the hundreds: 7 − 3 = 4

Crossing a ten: use the next ten

Sometimes the ones go past 10. Then jump to the next ten first, and add the rest.

Example

What is 352 − 7?

Jump back 2 to the ten: 352 − 2 = 350. 7 is 2 + 5, so take away 5 more: 350 − 5 = 345.

Answer: 345

Crossing a hundred: exchange 10 tens

10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. When the tens go past 10, exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred.

Example

What is 412 − 30?

412 has only 1 ten. Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens: 3 hundreds and 11 tens. 11 tens − 3 tens = 8 tens.

Answer: 382

Check with the inverse

Addition and subtraction undo each other. If 347 + 6 = 353, then 353 − 6 = 347.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding to the wrong digit: 347 + 6 = 947 or 4076 is 6 ones. Add it to the ones: 353
Not crossing the ten: 347 + 6 = 3437 + 6 = 13, so the tens go up by 1: 353
Taking the smaller digit from the larger: 352 − 7 = 355Jump back to 350, then 5 more: 345
Forgetting the exchange: 412 − 30 = 482Exchange 1 hundred, so 4 hundreds become 3: 382
Not crossing the hundred: 384 + 50 = 33413 tens is 1 hundred and 3 tens: 434

faq.q: What mental maths should a Year 3 child be able to do?
faq.a: The National Curriculum says Year 3 children should add and subtract in their heads a three-digit number and ones, tens or hundreds, such as 347 + 6, 412 − 30 and 526 + 300.

faq.q: How do you add a three-digit number and ones mentally?
faq.a: If the ones go past 10, jump to the next ten first. For 347 + 6, add 3 to make 350, then add the other 3 to get 353.

faq.q: What does exchange mean in Year 3 maths?
faq.a: Exchange means swapping 10 ones for 1 ten, or 10 tens for 1 hundred. For 412 − 30, exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens so there are 11 tens, then take away 3 tens to get 382.

faq.q: What maths do Year 3 children learn?
faq.a: Year 3 covers numbers to 1,000, mental and column addition and subtraction, the 3, 4 and 8 times tables, fractions, measures, money, time, shapes, and bar charts and pictograms.

items.q: You add 400 to 238. Which digit changes?
items.e: 400 is 4 hundreds, so only the hundreds digit changes: 238 + 400 = 638.

items.q: You take away 20 from 465. Which digit changes?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens, and 465 has 6 tens. Only the tens digit changes: 465 − 20 = 445.

items.q: Add 10, then take away 1. What is 456 + 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 less than 10. 456 + 10 = 466. Then 466 − 1 = 465. (466 forgets to take away 1.)

items.q: Take away 10, then add 1. What is 532 − 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 less than 10. 532 − 10 = 522. You took away 1 too many, so add it back: 522 + 1 = 523.

items.q: A library has 346 books. 7 new books arrive. How many books are there now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 346 + 4 = 350. 7 is 4 + 3, so add 3 more: 350 + 3 = 353.

items.q: Ava walks 485 steps to the park gate. She walks 8 more steps to the swings. How many steps is that?
items.e: Put the steps together, so add. Make the next ten first. 485 + 5 = 490. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 490 + 3 = 493.

items.q: A school has 423 pupils. 30 pupils go on a school trip. How many pupils stay at school?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 423 has 2 tens. You cannot take 3 tens from 2. Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens: 3 hundreds and 12 tens. 12 tens − 3 tens = 9 tens. 423 − 30 = 393.

items.q: Jack is on page 268 of a book. He reads 50 more pages. Which page is he on now?
items.e: Read on, so add. Tens: 6 tens + 5 tens = 11 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 2 to 3, and 1 ten is left. 268 + 50 = 318.

items.q: A shop has 615 stickers. It sells 200 stickers. How many stickers are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 200 is 2 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 6 − 2 = 4. The other digits stay the same. 615 − 200 = 415.

items.q: A football match has 834 fans. 300 fans leave early. How many fans are still watching?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 300 is 3 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 8 − 3 = 5. The other digits stay the same. 834 − 300 = 534.

items.q: A train has 408 seats. 9 seats are empty. How many seats have people in them?
items.e: Take the empty seats away, so subtract. Go back to the ten first. 408 − 8 = 400. 9 is 8 + 1, so take away 1 more: 400 − 1 = 399.

items.q: A garden centre has 572 plants. It sells 60 plants. How many plants are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 60 is 6 tens. Only the tens digit changes: 7 − 6 = 1. The other digits stay the same. 572 − 60 = 512.

items.q: George has 695 points in a game. He wins 8 more points. How many points does he have now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 695 + 5 = 700. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 700 + 3 = 703.

items.q: A bakery bakes 380 rolls in the morning and 40 rolls in the afternoon. How many rolls is that?
items.e: Put the two amounts together, so add. Tens: 8 tens + 4 tens = 12 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 3 to 4, and 2 tens are left. 380 + 40 = 420.

items.q: There are 517 books on the shelves. Pupils borrow 300 books. How many books are still on the shelves?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 300 is 3 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 5 − 3 = 2. The other digits stay the same. 517 − 300 = 217.

items.q: Evie has 452 stamps. Freya has 30 more stamps than Evie. How many stamps does Freya have?
items.e: 30 more than means add 30. 30 is 3 tens. Only the tens digit changes: 5 + 3 = 8. The other digits stay the same. 452 + 30 = 482.

items.q: There are 245 cars in a car park. 9 more cars drive in. How many cars are there now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 245 + 5 = 250. 9 is 5 + 4, so add 4 more: 250 + 4 = 254.

items.q: Grace runs 760 m. Then she runs 50 m more. How far does she run altogether?
items.e: Put the two distances together, so add. Tens: 6 tens + 5 tens = 11 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 7 to 8, and 1 ten is left. 760 + 50 = 810.

items.q: A book has 300 pages. Amelia has read 270 pages. How many pages are left?
items.e: Count on from 270 to 300: 7 tens + 3 tens = 10 tens. So 30 pages are left. Check: 270 + 30 = 300.

items.q: Isla has 548 beads. She gives away 6 beads. Then she buys 30 more. How many beads does she have now?
items.e: Step 1: 548 − 6 = 542. Step 2: 542 + 30 = 572. (578 adds the 6 instead of taking it away.)

items.q: A comic costs £2.45. A rubber costs 8p. Leo buys both. How much does he spend?
items.e: Buying both means add. Work in pence: £2.45 = 245p. Make the next ten first. 245 + 5 = 250. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 250 + 3 = 253. So the answer is 253p = £2.53.

items.q: Charlie has £5.12. He spends 40p on a pencil. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Spending means subtract. Work in pence: £5.12 = 512p. 512 has 1 ten. You cannot take 4 tens from 1. Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens: 4 hundreds and 11 tens. 11 tens − 4 tens = 7 tens. 512 − 40 = 472. So the answer is 472p = £4.72.

items.q: Poppy has £3.60 in her money box. Gran gives her £2. How much does she have now?
items.e: Getting more means add. Work in pence: £3.60 = 360p. 200 is 2 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 3 + 2 = 5. The other digits stay the same. 360 + 200 = 560. So the answer is 560p = £5.60.

items.q: Noah has £4.03. He spends 6p on sweets. How much money does he have left?
items.e: Spending means subtract. Work in pence: £4.03 = 403p. Go back to the ten first. 403 − 3 = 400. 6 is 3 + 3, so take away 3 more: 400 − 3 = 397. So the answer is 397p = £3.97.
